notes: Set at MEASURED CURRENT, not at an aspiration. Rebased 2026-10-16 when the coverage MEASURE changed to product code only: [tool.coverage.run] source in pyproject.toml now limits it to pa_core/, dashboard/ and design-system/, and tests, docs, scripts/, .github/ and the other tooling no longer count (owner decision 2026-10-16). Measured 84.02% on that basis (Gate run 38964793528; 84.0% to one decimal) and floored to 84, with warn_drop 1.0 absorbing run-to-run jitter. This is a change of basis, not a lowered floor and not a regression: the same code read 88.81% while every imported file counted (the tests' own ~98% among them), and the previous 86.0 (set 2026-08-26 at 86.25%) belongs to that old basis. Readings from before 2026-10-16 are not comparable with readings after it. A baseline above reality is red on arrival and gets switched off; one far below it cannot fail -- stranske/Fine-Art-Archive carried 25 against a real 81.45%, and stranske/Workflows carried 85 against a real 76.72% (both as measured 2026-08-26). Both are the same defect in opposite directions. This file is what lets Maint Coverage Guard compare at all: without it tools/coverage_trend.py reports baseline_status=absent and computes no delta. Keyed `line` because both coverage_trend.py and coverage_guard.py accept `line` or `coverage`, with `line` taking precedence. Raise it as coverage rises; it is a ratchet, not a target, and it is never lowered to make a run pass.
